## Why this unit matters

Move public URLs behind one entry point. Compare reverse proxies and gateways, then add route matching, filters, authentication and rate limits.

The same shop remains the anchor: Product owns catalogue information, User owns customer information, and Order coordinates checkout. Read each chapter in order to see which new requirement motivates the next design decision.

2. **[Nginx: Reverse Proxy and Routing](nginx-routing.qmd)**
3. **[Netflix Zuul Gateway](zuul-gateway.qmd)**
4. **[Spring Cloud Gateway](spring-cloud-gateway.qmd)**
5. **[Gateway Authentication, Rate Limiting, and Availability](gateway-auth-and-limits.qmd)**

## Learning objective

After this unit, describe the dependency or operational problem **before** naming a framework; draw the relevant call/event path; state the failure mode and trade-off; and explain how the concept applies to a small TypeScript or NestJS service.

## Mathematical Abstraction

A gateway maps a public route to an internal destination.

$$
g:(\mathrm{path},\mathrm{method},\mathrm{context})\mapsto \mathrm{upstream}
$$

$g$ is a route-resolution function; an unmatched or unauthorised request may result in rejection instead.
